headline: Record profit as pricing discipline offsets softer volumes
summary_short: Old Dominion's Q2 revenue rose 10.4% y/y to $1.55B as a 15.2% gain in LTL revenue per hundredweight offset a 4.1% drop in LTL tons per day, while the operating ratio improved 450bp to 70.1% and diluted EPS climbed 32.3% to $1.68, matching the company's prior quarterly record.
summary_long: Revenue growth was almost entirely price-driven: LTL revenue per hundredweight rose 15.2% (+5.5% ex-fuel), offsetting a 4.1% drop in LTL tons per day (shipments -5.7%, weight/shipment +1.7%). Operating ratio improved 450bp to 70.1%, aided by a 230bp gain in direct operating costs as a percent of revenue and $17.2M of net gains on equipment disposals. Net income rose 30.5% y/y to $351M; diluted EPS rose 32.3% to $1.68, tying the prior quarterly record. Cash was $284M at quarter-end after $239.7M of H1 buybacks and $120.7M of dividends. Management guides FY2026 capex to ~$380M.

Operating ratio improved 450bp to 70.1% on a 230bp gain in direct operating costs as a percent of revenue and improved overhead costs, aided by $17.2M of net gains on equipment disposals.
Management attributes the increase to the combination of revenue growth and operating-ratio improvement described above.
Tracks the net income increase; diluted EPS growth (32.3%) modestly outpaces net income growth (30.5%) due to a 1.6% reduction in weighted average diluted shares from the buyback program.

CEO cites continued improvement in demand trends and the benefits of the company's long-term focus on yield discipline and operational execution, alongside 99% on-time service and a 0.1% claims ratio.
